reference_memory.normal_pattern: The channel exhibits a robust quasi-periodic pattern with a fundamental period of ~92 points, as confirmed by the reference_cycle_plan and catalog. Across candidates, the waveform consists of smooth, asymmetric sawtooth-like cycles: each cycle rises gradually over ~60–70 points (positive slope ~0.001–0.009 per point), then falls sharply over ~20–30 points (steeper negative slope). Peaks are rounded and relatively consistent in height (robust standardized value ~1.0–2.0), while troughs are sharper and more variable (~−1.0 to −2.0), occasionally punctuated by narrow, high-magnitude spikes (up to ±2.2) that appear transient and localized. Baseline level drifts slowly (median shifts from −0.20 to +0.27 across candidates), but local stability within each window is high—noise is low-amplitude, high-frequency jitter (MAD ~0.47–0.67), not chaotic. Roughness and curvature metrics are uniformly low (0.1349), indicating smooth monotonic segments between inflection points. Amplitude at the 90th percentile is stable (~2.16–2.43), suggesting bounded variability. No sustained trends dominate; apparent slopes are minor and reversible. Boundary truncation is minimal—cycles are mostly完整 (especially in 3P and 5P windows), confirming the period estimate. Acceptable variation includes modest baseline offset, slight asymmetry in rise/fall duration, and occasional isolated spikes (<3σ) that do not disrupt the underlying cycle structure.

reference_memory.selection_guidance: Prefer candidate 2 for high-fidelity morphology matching (highest reliability, smoothest cycles); use candidate 1 when needing to recognize deeper troughs or transient dips; use candidate 3 for queries with 5+ cycles or when assessing long-range stability; candidate 0 is best for single-cycle alignment or boundary-sensitive tasks. Avoid using candidate 0 alone for amplitude/trend inference due to limited context.
uncertainties: Exact phase alignment of spikes relative to cycle position is not fully deterministic—some spikes appear at peak, others at trough; whether this is intrinsic or noise remains ambiguous.
Baseline drift magnitude across windows (−0.20 to +0.27) may reflect true slow trend or segmentation artifact; cannot confirm stationarity beyond local windows.
Whether the sharp mid-cycle drops are part of normal dynamics or rare micro-anomalies cannot be resolved without labels; consensus treats them as normal due to recurrence.
